risks.description: An approval is acknowledged (HTTP 200) but the record is held only in memory and is lost when the api process restarts, so the durably-recorded approval promised by AC-APPROVAL-002 disappears on the next read.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 approval state survives a re-read of persisted state; builder changed an approval endpoint with persistent state; gen-persist-approve only checks the write, not survival across a process restart.

risks.description: Two approval requests for the same invoice arriving simultaneously each write a durable approval record, producing a duplicated/divergent approval that breaks the store invariant.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 approving an invoice records the approval durably; gen-idempotent-approve failed (C01), suggesting the once-only guarantee is not solid, and no covered scenario exercises a true simultaneous race.

risks.description: Posting an approval for an invoice id that was never created records a phantom approval instead of rejecting it, corrupting persisted state.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 scopes durable recording to approving an invoice; nothing promises recording approvals for unknown invoices.

risks.description: A malformed approval request body causes a partial or spurious state mutation (or a 500) rather than a clean rejection with no persisted effect.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 requires durable recording of a valid approval; an endpoint that mutates state on garbage input violates the durable-record contract.

risks.description: Idempotency is enforced only in the live process, so re-approving the same invoice after a restart creates a second durable approval — the once-only guarantee does not survive persistence.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 approval state survives a re-read; gen-idempotent-approve (C01) already failed once in-process, so the across-restart case is higher risk.

expected_observations: Re-approve after restart 200 and still approved
forbidden_observations: SMOKE reports a duplicated/second approval for inv-idr5

assumptions: The approval endpoint is reachable as POST /api/invoices/{id}/approve on http://127.0.0.1:8961; if the real path differs, request-status assertions will need adjustment but the persisted-state evidence remains the load-bearing check.

unresolved_questions: The earlier idempotency failure (C01) asserted 'payments=<n>', which is not present in state.py output — it is unclear whether this product records 'payments' at all or only 'approvals'. If a payment side-effect is actually promised, that requirement is not stated in the ACs shown and should be clarified rather than assumed.

No product requirement defines the correct status code for approving an unknown invoice or for malformed input; 404/400 are assumptions, and the durable-state assertions are the true pass/fail signal.
